items.summary: Round-up of Belgrave road running from late 1986 to January 1988, with Martyn Head named Road Section Secretary, Gary Staines' wins on the Continent, team results and full club results from races including the London Marathon, Hogs Back and City 10 Miles.
items.text:
ROAD RACE ROUND UP

The odd success is coming the way of the road runners as efforts are being made to consolidate our entries for open races and word is spread of who is doing what! However communications still need improving if we are to do ourselves justice. There are so many races available these days that we should regularly be able to pick up some team prizes. It doesn't even need our very best men to be involved although we still look to them for a lead. A word in the right ear could enable us to get the back up brigade to join in and everyone could benefit. The guys running down the field will make that much more of an effort if they know there's something in it at the end. Martyn Head is your new Section Secretary. Contact him on [phone number withheld].

Two successes missed the boat for the last edition. These were the win in the City of London 10 Miles, where Don Anderson in 5th was a late entry non scorer, and in the Alton 10 Miles where Martin Lake, who was the holder, led the team home in 2nd place this time. In the Fleet Half Marathon, John Wright was representing the Army and didn't score for us but he finished 10th in a fast time with some respectable running behind from our team which placed 8th. Best performance in the London Marathon came from Canadian Peter Anthony who moves into 25th place in the club all time list with his time. Another prominent showing came from Dave North with a 2nd place in the Portsmouth 10 Miles in May in 54.22. Must have been tough, long or both Dave! Some of the best performances of the late Summer came in the breakthrough of 1984 Olympic cyclist Peter Sanders as you can see from the results below. Pete has now completed his first year as a runner and he looks to have plenty of potential. When he lined up alongside John Wright in the Brighton 6, there was a good chance of high placings from the pair and thats how it turned out, with John winning in 30.03 and Pete in 3rd. Unfortunately there was no back up for what would have been an easy team prize.

25.12.86 Lauriston Paarlauf: 1 J Gladwin & A Gayton 6m 909y 2 F Ward & M Peace(Ran) 6m 691y 3 M Riley & A Painter 6m 617y 4 P Sanders & J Bicourt 6m 548y 6 J Booth & S Williams 6m 436y

Other good performances in the second half of the year have come from Martin Lake, 3rd in the Wimbledon Half Marathon and Dave North one place behind but running for his firm and not counting for our team which finished 3rd. Richard Pearson collected the Club marathon title in the Poly Marathon where he was first Veteran home.

Gary Staines has continued his Summer track form into a Winter road season on the Continent in sensational fashion. On 11 October he was 2nd over 7.6km in Furth (WG) in a time of 20.21 and 16 days later smashed a World class field over 10km in Rennes (Fra) in 28.28. Koskei, Rousseau and Nyambui being just some of the names behind him. Then on 29 November he beat another International line up over a 7.4 mile course in Madrid in 32.55.58. That's an average of 4.27 per mile!

On the same weekend that Gary was winning in Madrid, John Wright won the Basingstoke '6' in 29.41 and Stuart Paton won a 5 miler in Epsom nearly 2 minutes clear of the field which included Chris Knight in 4th place.

items.heading: Young Athletes Report
items.summary: Jim and Dave Mote's report on the 1987 young athletes' league season (Belgrave 8th of 17 in the South Central Division), match by match with Belgrave winners and scores, plus a note on the Belgrave Thameside League for Colts and Boys.
items.text:
Young Athletes Report by Jim and Dave Mote

Out came the Wellingtons, Waterproofs and Umbrellas. In went the Sun. Yes it was the summer season again.

The 1987 Young Athletes season started with the traditional enthusiasm and expectation. Cross-Country runners chipped the dried mud from their spikes and the sprinters blew the cobwebs off theirs. All prepared for the season's first engagement at Tooting Bec.

3rd MAY 1987 TOOTING BEC

Dark clouds greeted us at Tooting Bec and it was not long before the new centenary umbrellas were in use and greatly appreciated by all who huddled under them. It was good to see some new faces mingling with the stalwarts from last year but a head count soon showed that our Boys and Youths teams were far from strong in numbers and the Colts section was almost non-existent.

Nevertheless everyone competed with great enthusiasm and after a long wet afternoon the fine efforts of our team were eventually beaten by the superior numbers of the athletes from the recently amalgamated Swale Combined Club. We managed to stay ahead of our South London rivals Herne Hill but sadly missed our Youth sprinters.

Winners for Belgrave.

Youths A Grant 400m Hurdles (A) 100m Hurdles (A)
J Coy 400m Hurldes (B), M Bowers 800m (A)
S Herbert 800m (B) 4 x 400m Relay

Boys W Chu 100m (A) 200m (A), M Burnett 100m (B)
S Abbeysinger 400m (A), D Parr 400m (B), B Khan 800m (B)
P Dunn Javelin (B), G Dorrell Discus (B) 4 x 400m Relay

Final Result - Swale 155, Belgrave 129, Herne Hill 123, Southwark 65, Haywards Heath 43

24th MAY 1987 BATTERSEA PARK

Our home match was our chance to show our mettle but on a warm afternoon with everyone expecting we would prove victorious we somehow let it slip and finished second. Once again we were pipped at the post by a team that could field more athletes on the day. Our faithful nucleus ran, jumped and threw with great gusto but were beaten by the numerical superiority of Kingston and Polytechnic Harriers.

Winners for Belgrave.

Youths A Grant 400m Hurdles (A) 100m Hurdles (A), M Bowers 1500m (A), R Blick 1500m (B), N Khan 800m (B) 4 x 400m Relay.

Boys S Abbeysinger 200m (B) 800m (A) Highjump (A)
G Bage 1500m (A), M Loftus 400m (A), D Cooper 400m (B)
B Khan 3000m (B), G Dorrell Hammer (A) Shot (A) Discus (B)
S Affleck Triple Jump (B), W Chu Discus (A) 4 x 400m Relay

Colts M Pettigrew 1500 (B)

Final Result Kingston & Poly 154, Belgrave 147, Hastings 83, Tonbridge 37

7th JUNE 1987 DARTFORD

On another dull threatening day we set off by coach to Dartford with a team which this time had only five youths and one Colt but our spirits were high and an impromptu game of cricket preceded the athletic match. Unfortunately our lack of numbers again made the match an uphill task from the very beginning but once again enthusiasm countered these problems and once again we finished second. An added bonus was the fact that the rain which threatened us all the afternoon never materialised and there was an air of satisfaction amongst the tired athletes on the journey home.

Winners from Belgrave

Youths A Grant 400m Hurdles (A) 100m Hurdles (A)

Boys S Affleck Triple Jump (B), S Herbert High Jump (A)
B Khan Long Jump (B), J Harris 100m Hurdles (A)
4 x 100m Relay

Colts M Loden 1500m (A)

Final Result Invicta 255, Belgrave 117, Ashford 87

28th JUNE 1987 HORSHAM

The sun came out! So shocked were the team that only 10 athletes turned out. Outnumbered by Belgrave parents, coaches, officials and other sundry supporters and not to mention the other teams, our athletes manfully battled against insurmountable odds. Just to add to our problems the three teams we were opposing were Bexley and E Grinstead who were at that time first and second in the league and Horsham who were the host club.
Apparently we were hit by the holiday season (not applicable to our opponents) and our results reflected the depleted nature of the team. But we all came home with a lovely sun-tan!

Our only individual winner was S Abbeysinger in the Boys High Jump (B).

Final Result (1) E Grinstead 268 (2) Bexley 2445
(3) Horsham 90 (4) Belgrave 58

26th JULY 1987 TOOTING BEC

Our final match on a fine afternoon gave us our best team in numbers of the whole season but still it was not strong enough. Our close rivals Hercules Wimbledon and Surrey Beagles had even bigger teams and after H.W. had taken a commanding lead early on we engaged in a close battle with Surrey Beagles for second place before losing our grip when our athletes had competed in their maximum number of events and left the Beagles to pick up the spare points. For the first time this season we had competitors in the Youth sprints but still failed to field a sprint relay team.

Winners for Belgrave

Youths A Grant 400m (A), R Blick 1500m (A) 1500m S/C (A)
J Coy 1500m (B), M Egericx 3000m (A), J French 100m (B)

Final Result Hercules Wimbledon 217, Surrey Beagles 149
Belgrave 121, Redhill 19

Seventeen teams competed in our South Central Division and Belgrave finished 8th.

It has been a hit and definitely miss season in which the consistent nucleus has performed with commendable enthusiasm and enjoyed their individual achievements. Unfortunately some of our talented athletes have been unable to attend on many occasions for various legitimate reasons and this is where our weakness lies Baba and Nadu Khan, Dan Winson, John Coy (Team Captain) and Michael Bowers competed in every match and I would like to thank them for their unswerving loyalty. In reporting the matches above I note that Dan Winson does not appear as a winner at any time but he is a winner in a different because he was always there always finished and always scored valuable points - well done Dan!! Another special mention goes to Michael Bowers our up and coming middle distance runner who injured his foot and could not run in the second part of the season - he came along and "shot-putted" instead!! What more can one say?!

Think about it lads. You have a great deal of talent. A little more consistency in your appearances and the league could be yours for the taking. And finally many, many thanks to the parents, coaches, officials and would-be officials who supported us (not forgetting the supporters from the ladies section who graced us with their presence on many occasions). Have a good winter season and come back fit and raring to go!

Belgrave Thameside League

This league was an interesting innovation five years ago when Belgrave decided to provide additional competition for the younger boys in some local clubs. Its development has been quite remarkable with four very competitive meetings taking place over the short athletic season. Our own teams (Colts and Boys) have not been once sucessful in the competition but have enjoyed the opportunity to compete in a league with surprisingly high standards. On average the turn out of Belgrave athletes was better this year and one encouraging aspect was the increase in the number of Colts taking part. Only two arrived for the first match but by the last one our team had grown to eight.

Six teams competed in each of the divisions both of which were won by Croydon. Our Boys finished fourth and the Colts were fifth but we have great hopes of improving on this next year.

A number of Belgrave officials work very hard to present this competition and must be applauded on the high standard they have achieved. We trust the Belgrave athletes will show their appreciation of these efforts with an even greater and more consistent turn-out next year.

Jim and David Mote

items.heading: BELGRAVIAN WALKING SECTION REPORT
items.summary: Carl Lawton's Walking Section report on the 1987 summer and autumn season, race by race with Belgrave results from the Battersea 10km track championships to the Chippenham to Calne 6 miles in October.
items.text:
Race Walking.

BELGRAVIAN WALKING SECTION REPORT by Carl Lawton

The summer is past and in certain cases that may be a good thing. As far as some results go it has been disastrous and well worth forgetting but all is not doom and gloom, we have now a rebuilt ladies team which has got what has been lacking in the means section, a desire to be successful, but even that is only dependant on turning out a team. Suzanne Kew has been 'sidelined' during the summer but hopes to be back on the road having sorted out her problem.

The Nation 35kms and 50kms failed to close in a team the latter even a finisher. September began to look a little more hopeful with teams in the Woodford and Southend.

We did think we might have a junior team in the making but as so often happens more exciting things came along and they were lost.

items.heading: WITH THE LADIES
items.summary: Harry Porter's review of the Belgrave ladies' 1987 season: Angela Abrams' Endeavour Cup, Southern multi and relay medals, Rosenheim League and Melbourne Trophy wins, Frances Guy's Centenary Cup, Frank Simmons' recovery, and thanks to helpers.
items.text:
The Ladies.

WITH THE LADIES

It has been quite an exciting track season, I hope everybody in the 'SECT' has had an exciting centenary one as I've had myself and are looking forward to the '88 summer season.

Of the team I would like to see back in competition in '88 are Tracy Denton and Andrea Coore, both out last year, we all missed you and your points. I hope the back and leg hold out OK good luck to both for '88.

I would also like to thank Angela Abrams for her enthusiasm, and sportswomen-like attitude and support for the team, Angela holds all four club records for 80/100/200/400/H. Keep it up Angela (it's electric) for this and all the support to the club, you have been awarded the "Endeavour Cup" good luck for '88 (GB vest??)

There are numerous individual performances throughout the year Juniors and Seniors as you will see later. But one of the best days for us was when we went down to Bournemouth for the Southern CW AAA multi and relays championships. We came away with a total of (11 Gold) (1 Silver) (8 Bronze) and 5 Club records.

Our Juniors relay team won both the 4 x 100 and 4 x 200. I would like to say well done on behalf of the club on doing the sprint double a first for Belgrave ladies, well done. Keep it up.

We also won the Rosenheim League final at Tooting Bec on 19th August. This was the first time the ladies teams have taken part, as before it was a mens league only so Belgrave ladies hold the trophy. The mens team just missing the double by about 2 pts? But it was good fun on the night, well done all. It's good to see the ladies and means team getting together more.

Also later at the end of the season on 20th September Belgrave were invited to take part in the Melbourne Trophy meeting at Crystal Palace, where 15 teams took part, there were good performances all round so we found ourselves in 3rd place overall. But we did end up first GB club so that itself was very pleasing. With France 1st, Belgium 2nd, Belgrave 3rd, with 12 more GB clubs behind us, we were awarded the 1987 home club Melbourne Trophy for top GB club on the day. Well done all, keep it up, it's there if you wish to use it? But if it's not then you did even better as a certain Mr Frank Simmons would say.

On the 4th of October or before we had a full team for the 25x1 mile relay at Battersea but 3 or 4 ladies failed to show on the day so sadly we did not have a scoring team so some had to run 2 legs to record a time to be bettered next year? With a full team I hope.

But for me the run of the day was by one of the sprinters (Dez) well what can one say Dezrine a 6m.mile, behind the sub 4m of Gary Staines, yours for me was second to that. Ask poor old Charles Manning I think he is still running (full team for '88 ladies please). We missed out on the day by £350.

On 14 November we held the Centenary Dinner at the Gloucester Hotel. At this prestigious occasion the Tommy Green Cup was awarded for the most or best performance by a male athlete, also for the first time was presented a new cup which is named the Centenary Cup to be awarded to the lady for the best performance of the year. The first name on the cup in centenary year is Frances Guy for her win in the Poly Marathon incorporating also the Belgrave Marathon. Well done Frances from the Sec and myself.

Just a few words about one of the older Belgravians of the club, he is just what makes the club one of the great ones that it is, we don't have more than 10 or so of them left and we so very nearly lost this one in September. For ten days 90% of him was with all those Bels who have passed on, but 10% said not yet sir, for three weeks he battled on in the intensive care unit. Many younger men would have lost this race but he kept on striding on and won. His willpower and spirit is something to be admired by all who know him, those of you who don't know him or of him his name is Frank Simmons, and Frank I would like to shake your hand and say on behalf of Belgrave Harriers please accept the merit award for willpower you old so-and-so.

P.S. To the doctors and nurses at the East Dulwich Hospital I would like to thank you all for your dedication and care on behalf of Frank and myself.

Finally I would like to say thank you to all those people who have given the Ladies Section and myself so much help throughout the year and in particular to Derek Jones for organising all the track meetings and all the back-room work that he does (without question or having to be asked) - "Stick with it Derek", to Cynthia and Ray James, Jenny and Chris Christou, Derek Crookes, the club officials and that small band of officials and that small band of officials that regularly turn out. The club needs many more like you so please if you can help in any capacity, qualified or not do come forward.

I would like to thank the Club President Bill Lucas and Sheena his wife, for their support, at several of our home and away fixtures - hope to see you again in 1988 season.

Well ladies, the section is numerically stronger but we failed Div 1 and 2 in Centenary year. It must be on for 1988 - you have all to get it together and you can. So let's make it a "super" 1 and 3 this year. Well done all those who competed in 1987 - good luck for 1988.

Harry Porter
